title: Schemas & search_path Resolution
description: Organize database objects into schemas, configure search_path resolution, and implement multi-tenant schema isolation.

data.text: A **schema** in PostgreSQL is a namespace within a database that contains tables, views, functions, and types. By default, all objects are created in the `public` schema. Using custom schemas is common for modular architecture and multi-tenant SaaS applications.
When you execute `SELECT * FROM users`, PostgreSQL searches schemas in the order defined by the **`search_path`** parameter (analogous to the `PATH` environment variable in Linux).

data.title: Configuring search_path for Tenant Isolation
data.content: Switching schemas dynamically based on tenant.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Schemas act as namespaces inside a single database.
`search_path` dictates the resolution order of unqualified table names.
Multi-tenant schema patterns provide clean logical separation of customer data.
